newsitem.title: UK: UK's PCR sees cocoa deficit at 127,000 T in 96/97.
newsitem.headline: UK's PCR sees cocoa deficit at 127,000 T in 96/97.

text.p: UK cocoa analysts PCR Ltd estimated the cocoa supply deficit in 1996/97 (October-September) at 127,000 tonnes compared with a surplus of 186,000 tonnes seen in 1995/96, a PCR official said on Tuesday.
In a report issued for private clients on Monday, PCR estimated Ivory Coast's output at 1.065 million tonnes from 1.220 million seen in 1995/96.
It put Ghana's production at 345,000 tonnes from 410,000 and Brazil's at 197,000 from 236,000.
Total world production was pegged at 2.695 million tonnes, significantly lower than last season's estimate of 2.929 million.
PCR forecast world grindings at 2.795 million tonnes, representing an increase of three percent over 1995/96.
World stocks at the end of September were pegged at 1.078 million tonnes and the projected stocks/consumption ratio -- a barometer of prices -- at 39 percent, the lowest for ten years.
PCR said there was still uncertainties over the quantity of the early harvest in Ivory Coast amid conflicting reports about the volume of arrivals to date.
"PCR's best estimate of arivals is a little under 300,000 tonnes to 24th November and on this basis we would expect overall main crop production to be about 915,000 tonnes," according to the report.
Podsetting for the 1997 intermediate crop had barely started but the PCR estimated the Ivorian mid crop this season at 150,000 tonnes.
Ghana's main crop was estimated at 305,000 tonnes.
The report said some correction was due in cocoa prices after the anticipated supply deficit in the current season.

Prices would react to a decline in the stocks/consumption ratio from the 1995/96 estimate of 44 percent, but in the second half of 1997 prices would be influenced also by expectations for next season's main crop.

Assuming a four-percent trade-weighted depreciation of sterling and unchanged production for 1997/98, PCR forecast second-month London cocoa futures to average 1,135 stg a tonne in 1997, compared with 944 stg, basis the March contract on Tuesday.
"If on the other hand a crop of over 2.9 million tonnes were once again in contemplation for 1997/98, the average price might be expected to be around 1,070 stg," it added.
PCR estimated Nigeria's output at 133,000 tonnes in 1996/97, down from 143,000 the previous season.
